title: Ambiguous clock, dinner: the party counters "Thursday works better. Let's do 7." On a dinner plan 7 means 7pm; record the yes on Thursday 7pm and book.
source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee), EXCEPT the working hours: 7am to 9pm on weekdays in this world. With the captured policy (9 to 5) every 7am and every 7pm check is "outside Bob's working hours", so Winnie cannot schedule a breakfast or a dinner at all; that is a finding in itself (recorded in the notes).

review.answer: Bob, 2026-11-05: a bare 7 on a meal plan is enough to count as their yes. Revised 2026-11-07 (harness walkthrough): "that should be an explicit ask to me"; the loop asks Bob which reading he wants, and books only on his word.
review.question: "Let's do 7" on a dinner plan: the rules (and the V1 grader) say a bare 7 is not a clock, so she proposes Thursday at 7pm and waits for the yes. Should a bare hour count as their yes when the plan's shape leaves one reading, so she books it directly?

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find us an evening for dinner next week,
somewhere between 5:30 and 9? I'll book Place 5. Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up dinner with you at Place 5. Here are times that work on his side:

- Mon, Nov 16, 6:30pm to 8:00pm ET
- Tue, Nov 17, 6:45pm to 8:15pm ET
- Fri, Nov 20, 6:00pm to 7:30pm ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

sent.summary: Offered three dinner times at the place Bob named, Bob in cc.

events.trigger: Noel Brandt replied on the thread.

thread.text: Thursday works better for me. Let's do 7.

bobDecides.what: whether a bare "7" on a dinner plan means 7pm

expect.basis: Bob's ruling (harness walkthrough, 2026-11-07): a bare "7" on a dinner plan is an explicit ask to him, not a yes to record. She tells him what was written and which reading the plan's shape gives (7pm, Thu Nov 19 19:00), and books on his word. His 11-05 ruling (a bare 7 is enough for a yes) is superseded.
expect.notes: EDGE: Winnie's yes-guard (tools.ts namesAClock) refuses a bare "7" as a clock, which is the right first step; the gap is the next one. At 34013da the loop then proposes the 7pm slot back to the party (C, 5 of 5) and, with the guard shadowed, books it (B, 5 of 5). Build request 5: after a refused bare-hour yes on a meal plan, ask Bob which reading he wants. A record_yes or book here settles his call (V6). The dinner band is the plan's own (ask-shape earliest and latest).
